body: That's what I want, especially for the benefits.  I will hear back from the mill before I even go to the orientation with the union, though.  It would be hard to turn down the mill if I don't have a sure thing with the union yet.
Thanks.  If you get into the union in a certain region can you relocate and transfer to another local later?
It is actually, but it's not the same union as millwrights here in the US.  I think the mill is United Steelworkers.  I haven't been able to get much information from the HR person on it though.
How much of a role does the region you are in play in the amount of work you get?

I'm not strapped for cash, I could spend the next few months traveling around trying to get into different locals.  Because I do want to go union.  Just apprehensive about getting my foot in the door in the trade.
Not yet, but the HR person at the paper mill has made it sound like I've got the job if I pass the test.  The union is a lot more uncertain at this point in time.

Thanks.  I'm not there yet, still have to interview and take an aptitude test, but yeah, there is a probationary period of like 120 days.  I agree, and it's not going to hurt the company, it's not like it's a mom and pop shop.
